claims.text: The starting material is a nanoscale coating composed of alternating FCC and BCC high-entropy-alloy layers with chemically homogeneous, intact interfaces.

Under sustained loading, plastic deformation is progressively mediated by a synergy between interface-inhibited dislocation motion and deformation-twin nucleation triggered by local elastic undulations.
FCC/BCC multilayer interfaces act as obstacles to dislocation glide.
The multilayer interfaces act as stress concentrators that promote a transition to twin-mediated plasticity.
Lattice distortion and high activation barriers impede dislocation motion at the multilayer interfaces.
Restricted dislocation motion creates localized internal-stress build-ups at the interfaces.
Nanoscale elastic-field undulations induced by internal stress act as precursors that trigger deformation-twin nucleation.
The resulting twin boundaries accommodate strain and interact with dislocations to enhance strain hardening while maintaining strength.

Relative to a homogeneous HEA coating, the multilayer will initially deform through impeded dislocation motion and subsequently develop an increasing density of deformation twins along its interfaces.
Elastic undulations and twin-boundary formation will be observable at the nanoscale during loading.
The proposed dual mechanism will maintain or enhance strength and improve strain hardening.
The multilayer will exhibit a moderate creep rate under sustained loading.
Plastic deformation in homogeneous non-multilayer HEA coatings is primarily governed by conventional dislocation slip without pronounced twinning.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the multilayer interfaces remain chemically and mechanically intact and no delamination or phase transformation occurs.
The transition stress and the quantitative contributions of dislocation slip and twinning remain uncertain and may vary with composition and loading conditions.

A failure to observe either a different progression of twinning or elastic undulations in multilayers versus homogeneous coatings, or a shift from dislocation- to twin-mediated plasticity, would falsify the mechanism.

contradictions.description: The protocol simultaneously describes controlled strain-rate conditions and constant-load creep. Strain rate is normally a measured response under constant load rather than an independently controlled variable, so the loading mode is internally ambiguous.
